pairs.subject: credential-vault
pairs.evidence: crates/server/src/routes/watches.rs:350 Slack watches retain their capability-bearing incoming-webhook URLs as ordinary database values and expose them through serialized watch responses, violating sealed custody and secret-free responses.

techniques.evidence: crates/server/src/routes/watches.rs:266 Watch listings serialize the complete Watch; its url field is serialized, including Slack incoming-webhook credentials, although the separate HMAC secret is excluded.

crates/core/src/storage.rs:1875 The watch creation path binds the supplied Slack incoming-webhook URL directly into SQLite without sealing; Storage::connect also configures an ordinary SQLite connection.
crates/server/src/webhook.rs:867 The traced watch transport uses a retained webhook URL directly; its retry loop retries message delivery, with no issuer lease or lease-extension operation.
crates/server/src/webhook.rs:171 The Slack branch formats and sends notifications directly to the stored endpoint; it does not proxy an issuer or cache leased secrets for consumers.
crates/server/src/routes/watches.rs:297 The retained Slack capability is an incoming-webhook URL, without a refresh-grant/access-proof pair in the admission, storage, or delivery path.

crates/server/src/webhook.rs:874 Delivery uses the supplied shared signing secret directly; this path neither mints a vault-owned sealing-key family nor provides versioned encryption or rewrap operations.
